papers.title: Integrative multi-omics profiling of insomnia-related molecular features reveals microbiome, immune, and therapy-relevant heterogeneity in colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Emerging evidence implicates insomnia as a potential risk factor in carcinogenesis, potentially involving systemic inflammation, circadian disruption, and microbiome alterations. However, the molecular associations linking insomnia-related features to colorectal cancer (CRC), particularly with respect to tumor biology, immune microenvironmental states, and therapy-relevant phenotypes, remain largely unexplored. Multi-omics integration of genomic, transcriptomic, and microbiome data from 3,026 CRC patients across seven independent cohorts, including a large, well-annotated Clinical Omics study
papers.summary: This study integrates genomic, transcriptomic, and microbiome data from 3,026 colorectal cancer patients across seven cohorts to characterize molecular features associated with insomnia. The authors identify insomnia-related signatures linked to immune microenvironment states, microbiome composition, and therapy-relevant phenotypes, revealing substantial heterogeneity among CRC patients. These findings suggest insomnia-related molecular features may have clinical implications for CRC stratification and treatment.

papers.title: Real-time volatilomics reveals microbiota and pathogen fingerprints in the honey bee.
papers.abstract: Understanding the complex relationship between gut microbiota and their hosts often relies on invasive sampling techniques. Honey bees provide a tractable model for host-microbe studies. Here, we establish single-bee volatilomics using secondary electrospray ionization-high-resolution mass spectrometry (SESI-HRMS) to examine volatile organic compounds released to the air around an individual live honey bee. Specifically, we focused on the primary gut microbiota metabolites present in gnotobiotic bees. Our findings reveal distinct volatilome profiles in honey bees that depend on their gut bacte
papers.summary: This study establishes a real-time, non-invasive method called single-bee volatilomics using SESI-HRMS to detect volatile organic compounds released by individual live honey bees. The researchers found that the volatile profiles differ depending on the bee's gut bacterial composition, allowing them to fingerprint both microbiota and pathogens without invasive sampling. This provides a new tool for studying host-microbe interactions in a tractable model organism.

papers.title: Genome-resolved analysis reveals disruption of gut microbial vitamin B and K2 biosynthesis during Toxoplasma gondii infection in mice.
papers.abstract: Toxoplasma gondii infection remodels the gut microbiome, yet its impact on microbial vitamin biosynthetic potential and host redox metabolism remains unclear. Here, we integrated mouse gut metagenomes with publicly available metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) to construct a genome-resolved atlas of B-vitamin and vitamin K2 biosynthesis. From 45,697 MAGs, we curated 4,771 representative genomes, of which 2,682 met high-quality criteria (completeness ≥90%, contamination <5%). Functional annotation identified 229,717 vitamin-related genes corresponding to 177 Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Geno
papers.summary: This study used genome-resolved metagenomics to map the biosynthetic potential for B vitamins and vitamin K2 in the mouse gut microbiome during Toxoplasma gondii infection. By curating thousands of high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes, the authors found that infection disrupts microbial vitamin biosynthesis pathways, which may contribute to altered host redox metabolism.

papers.title: ON-Time enables rapid microbiome sequencing and analysis for precision medicine.
papers.abstract: Clinical application of microbiome-guided therapies in the intensive care unit (ICU) requires a method to rapidly analyze patient microbiomes to guide urgent treatment decisions. Conventional microbiome sequencing and analysis methods require long turnaround times, methodological complexity, and high costs that are barriers to clinical application. Here, we describe a method for rapid (<5 h turnaround from sample to results) and accurate metagenomic sequencing and taxonomic analysis of microbiomes in individual patient fecal samples, called ON-Time. ON-Time uses a simplified and rapid wet-lab
papers.summary: ON-Time is a new method for rapid metagenomic sequencing and taxonomic analysis of patient fecal microbiomes, achieving sample-to-result turnaround in under 5 hours. It addresses the long turnaround times, complexity, and high costs of conventional microbiome sequencing that hinder clinical use in the ICU. This enables timely microbiome-guided treatment decisions for critically ill patients.

papers.title: Do Multi-Omics Approaches Improve the Diagnosis of Microbial Overgrowth Syndromes?
papers.abstract: This review investigates how advances in breath testing (BT), small bowel (SB) culture, metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, transcriptomics and proteomics are reshaping the definition and diagnosis of small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO). It also discusses whether SIBO should be redefined as part of a larger group of microbial overgrowth syndromes.
papers.summary: This review examines how emerging multi-omics technologies—including metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, transcriptomics, and proteomics—are changing the diagnosis and definition of small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO). It also considers whether SIBO should be reconceptualized as part of a broader category of microbial overgrowth syndromes rather than a single condition.

papers.title: Large-scale benchmarking of prokaryotic annotation tools across thousands of species.
papers.abstract: Genome annotation is an important step in deriving functional meaning from prokaryotic sequencing data, yet systematic evaluations guiding tool selection are lacking. We present the first large-scale investigation of four prominent open-source annotation tools (Prokka, Bakta, EggNOG-mapper, and PGAP) across 156,033 diverse genomes. This includes Escherichia coli strains for baseline performance, thousands of archaea and bacteria genomes, as well as frameshifted and metagenome-assembled genomes.
papers.summary: This study benchmarks four popular prokaryotic genome annotation tools (Prokka, Bakta, EggNOG-mapper, and PGAP) across 156,033 diverse genomes, including E. coli, archaea, bacteria, and challenging metagenome-assembled and frameshifted genomes. It provides the first large-scale systematic comparison to guide tool selection for prokaryotic annotation.

papers.title: Exploring the ecological drivers of bacteriophage diversity and functional viral potential in the skin of the axolotl Ambystoma altamirani.
papers.abstract: Bacteriophages play important roles in shaping microbial community dynamics across diverse environments. In the amphibian skin, most microbiome studies have focused on bacteria and their interactions with the fungus Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis (Bd), leaving other microbial components, including viruses, largely unexplored. Here, we present the first characterization of the viral community in the amphibian skin microbiome, focusing on ecological drivers of bacteriophage diversity and functional potential in the axolotl Ambystoma altamirani. Using public shotgun metagenomes, we found that the
papers.summary: This study provides the first characterization of the bacteriophage community in amphibian skin, using public shotgun metagenomes from the axolotl Ambystoma altamirani. It explores ecological drivers of phage diversity and functional potential, expanding beyond the bacterial-focused view of amphibian skin microbiomes and their role in Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis (Bd) interactions.

papers.title: Meta-CD: a metagenomic sequencing coverage and depth calculator for target species.
papers.abstract: Metagenomic Coverage and Depth Calculator (Meta-CD) is a convenient, biologist-friendly tool for determining coverage and depth to enhance taxonomic detection, functional profiling, and metagenome-assembled genome (MAG) recovery in metagenomics. It supports experimental design and post-sequencing analysis, modeling how genome size, relative abundance, sequencing depth, and DNA quantity influence detection of target species.
papers.summary: Meta-CD is a user-friendly tool that calculates sequencing coverage and depth for target species in metagenomic samples. It models how factors like genome size, relative abundance, sequencing depth, and DNA input quantity affect the detection of specific organisms, aiding both experimental design and post-sequencing analysis.

papers.title: Proteo-metabolomic integration identifies stage-specific candidate biomarkers for Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder with a prolonged prodromal phase and complex motor symptoms. Despite improved clinical criteria, early diagnosis and longitudinal monitoring remain challenging. While cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and plasma metabolites and proteins show biomarker potential, their utility in predictive models is insufficiently characterized. We employed a secondary computational approach to integrate proteometabolomic profiles from CSF and plasma samples of >1100 Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI) participants. Using multi-omics ma
papers.summary: This study computationally integrated proteomic and metabolomic data from cerebrospinal fluid and plasma of over 1,100 Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative participants to identify stage-specific candidate biomarkers. The multi-omics approach revealed distinct molecular signatures associated with different stages of Parkinson's disease, potentially improving early diagnosis and longitudinal monitoring. The findings highlight the value of combining protein and metabolite profiles for more accurate disease staging.

papers.title: Microbial content versus microbial interaction: the impact of medications on CF airway microbial ecosystems.
papers.abstract: The airways of people with cystic fibrosis (pwCF) are often colonized by a variety of different microbes. Although much effort has been put into cataloguing the impact of medication on the identities and abundances of these microbes, far less has been directed towards examining this from an ecological perspective, i.e., examining how medications affect the network and types of interactions between microbes.
papers.journal: Journal of cystic fibrosis : official journal of the European Cystic Fibrosis Society
papers.summary: This paper argues that research on how medications affect cystic fibrosis airway microbes has focused on which microbes are present and their abundances, rather than on the ecological interactions between them. The authors propose shifting to a network-based ecological perspective to better understand how treatments reshape microbial communities.

papers.title: The cystic fibrosis gut microbial dysbiosis index (CF-GMDI): a quantitative measure of gut microbial imbalance in children with cystic fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Gut dysbiosis is a hallmark of cystic fibrosis (CF), typically characterised using non-specific diversity metrics and study-specific taxonomic lists, limiting comparability across studies. We aimed to develop a metagenomic, species-level CF Gut Microbial Dysbiosis Index (CF-GMDI) to standardise measurement of gut microbial imbalance in children with CF (cwCF) METHODS: CF-GMDI was derived using stool metagenomic data from the PEARL-CF study (70 cwCF; 67 healthy controls (HC); 0-6 years). Differentially abundant taxa were identified between cwCF and HC using MaAsLin2. The index was calculated as
papers.journal: Journal of cystic fibrosis : official journal of the European Cystic Fibrosis Society
papers.summary: This study developed the CF-GMDI, a metagenomic species-level index that quantifies gut microbial dysbiosis in children with cystic fibrosis, derived from stool samples of 70 CF children and 67 healthy controls. The index uses differentially abundant taxa identified via MaAsLin2 to provide a standardized, comparable measure of microbial imbalance across studies, addressing the limitations of non-specific diversity metrics and study-specific taxonomic lists.

papers.title: Optimizing a culture-enriched hybrid metagenomics pipeline to assess the AMR footprint of livestock manure in anaerobic digestate.
papers.abstract: The role of environmental samples from livestock production systems, including manure and anaerobic digestate, as reservoirs of antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) is likely underestimated because conventional metagenomic approaches can overlook low-abundance ARGs and often lack the resolution to associate these genes with their microbial hosts and co-localized mobile genetic elements (MGEs). We evaluated whether culture-enriched metagenomics (CEMG), with and without antibiotic selection, enhances ARG detection in anaerobic digestate and improves the resolution of ARG-MGE-host associations u
papers.summary: This study evaluates a culture-enriched metagenomics (CEMG) pipeline, with and without antibiotic selection, to better detect antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) in livestock manure and anaerobic digestate. The approach aims to overcome the limitations of conventional metagenomics, which often misses low-abundance ARGs and struggles to link these genes to their microbial hosts and mobile genetic elements. The findings suggest that culture enrichment improves both ARG detection and the resolution of ARG-MGE-host associations in environmental samples.

papers.title: Identifying fundamental gaps in functional metagenomics: a step towards unlocking microbiome research potential.
papers.abstract: Incomplete functional annotation limits biological interpretation in microbiome studies and their translational potential. Poor annotation arises from multiple causes, with incomplete gene-protein-reaction mapping being one tractable yet under-examined contributor. We address this gap by developing a comprehensive hierarchical framework that systematically integrates gene families in UniRef, proteins in UniProt, and metabolic reactions in MetaCyc and BioCyc through UniProtKB accession, EC number, and Pfam-domain matching. Applied to a human gut metagenome dataset via HUMAnN3, our MetaCyc-based
papers.summary: This paper develops a hierarchical framework that links gene families (UniRef), proteins (UniProt), and metabolic reactions (MetaCyc/BioCyc) using UniProtKB accessions, EC numbers, and Pfam domains. Applying it to human gut metagenomes via HUMAnN3 reveals fundamental gaps in functional annotation that limit biological interpretation in microbiome studies. The work highlights incomplete gene-protein-reaction mapping as a tractable contributor to poor annotation and proposes a systematic approach to address it.

papers.title: Convergent methodologies in prosthetic joint infection research: integrating transdisciplinary approaches to understand and prevent biofilm-driven failure of orthopaedic prostheses.
papers.abstract: Prosthetic joint infections (PJIs) remain among the most devastating complications of arthroplasty, imposing substantial clinical, economic and patient burdens. Although culture-based diagnostics underpin current clinical practice, PJIs are biofilm-driven infections shaped by taxonomic diversity, spatial organization, host responses and surface interactions, meaning conventional approaches provide only a partial and often decontextualized view of the infection process. We examine how convergent methodologies can transform PJI research by integrating approaches that have traditionally been stud
papers.summary: This review argues that prosthetic joint infections (PJIs) are biofilm-driven processes that culture-based diagnostics fail to capture fully, because they ignore taxonomic diversity, spatial organization, host responses, and surface interactions. The authors propose integrating transdisciplinary methods—such as advanced imaging, multi-omics, and biofilm models—to better understand and prevent these orthopaedic implant failures.

papers.title: Benchmarking methods for extracting microbial signal from host-dominated metatranscriptomes.
papers.abstract: Human RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data originally generated for human transcriptome profiling are overwhelmingly dominated by host sequences, yet they often contain a small fraction of non-human reads that can be exploited for microbial detection. When such datasets are repurposed for secondary microbiome-oriented analyses, extracting and accurately classifying this weak microbial signal becomes technically challenging, and no ready-to-use pipeline currently exists. In this study, we evaluate computational strategies for filtering host reads and classifying microbial transcripts in host-dominated
papers.summary: This study benchmarks computational approaches for extracting weak microbial signals from human RNA-seq datasets that are overwhelmingly host-dominated. The authors evaluate host-read filtering and microbial transcript classification strategies, addressing the lack of a ready-to-use pipeline for repurposing human transcriptome data for microbiome analysis.

papers.title: Maternal secretor status and human milk oligosaccharides influence the infant gut resistome.
papers.abstract: The infant gut resistome is established early in life and is shaped by perinatal exposures, yet the mechanisms underlying its modulation remain unclear. We combined shotgun metagenomics of fecal samples from 57 one-month-old infants and paired milk samples from 50 mothers in the MAMI cohort to investigate the influence of maternal secretor status on early-life resistome development. Longitudinal follow-up at 6 and 12 months, and also further validation in the independent Lifelines NEXT (LLNEXT) cohort, support our findings. Cesarean section (C-section) was associated with increased antibiotic
papers.summary: This study shows that a mother's secretor status (whether she produces certain milk oligosaccharides) and the resulting human milk oligosaccharides in breast milk shape the community of antibiotic-resistance genes in her infant's gut. Using metagenomics from 57 one-month-old infants and their mothers, with validation in an independent cohort, the authors found that C-section delivery was linked to higher antibiotic resistance gene abundance, while maternal secretor status and milk oligosaccharides appear to modulate the early-life resistome.

papers.title: Comparative analysis of microbial communities, assembly processes, and life-history strategies in a mariculture-impacted eutrophic bay and adjacent coastal sediments.
papers.abstract: Coastal embayments are increasingly subjected to intensive mariculture, which delivers sustained nutrient, organic matter, and antibiotics to sediments, yet microbiome responses remain poorly understood. Here we compared sediment microbiomes of the eutrophic Xiangshan Bay (XSB) and oligotrophic East China Sea (ECS), integrating cell counts, 16S rRNA amplicon, metagenomics, and cultivation-based resistance assays. Cell counts and amplicon data showed that XSB harbored higher microbial abundance (1.28 ×108-1.34 ×109 vs. 2.07 ×107-4.43 ×108 cells g⁻¹), Chao1 richness (10,374-16,674 vs. 8311-12,28
papers.summary: This study compared sediment microbiomes between a eutrophic mariculture-impacted bay (Xiangshan Bay) and the oligotrophic East China Sea using cell counts, 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing, metagenomics, and cultivation-based resistance assays. The eutrophic bay harbored higher microbial abundance and richness, with distinct community assembly processes and life-history strategies, suggesting that mariculture-driven nutrient and antibiotic inputs substantially reshape sediment microbial ecology.

papers.title: Syndromic cholera diagnosis masks diverse causes of diarrhoeal disease in Burundi revealed by portable metagenomics.
papers.abstract: Cholera outbreaks remain a major public-health challenge in sub-Saharan Africa, where diagnostic capacity is limited and clinical case definitions are non-specific and re ly heavily on syndromic diagnosis. Rapid identification of Vibrio cholerae is critical, yet cholera-suspected diarrhoea can have multiple infectious causes not captured by targeted diagnostics.
papers.summary: This study used portable metagenomic sequencing to investigate diarrhoeal disease in Burundi, where cholera is typically diagnosed based on clinical symptoms alone. They found that many cases classified as cholera by syndromic diagnosis were actually caused by diverse other pathogens, revealing that reliance on clinical case definitions masks the true aetiology of diarrhoeal disease. Portable metagenomics proved feasible for pathogen identification in a low-resource outbreak setting.

papers.title: xoxF-linked methanol oxidation signals recur across wetland metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Wetlands are globally important methane-cycling ecosystems, but methanol oxidation remains less frequently emphasized than methane oxidation in community-level metagenomic analyses. Recent studies have highlighted the ecological importance of the lanthanide-dependent methanol dehydrogenase XoxF, yet wetland-focused xoxF literature remains comparatively limited relative to marine, freshwater, and other environmental systems. Here, we screened wetland-associated records in IMG/M using methane-metabolism and enzyme-centered queries focused on EC 1.1.2.10/xoxF and related methanol-oxidation annota
papers.summary: This study screened wetland metagenomes in the IMG/M database for genes involved in methanol oxidation, particularly the lanthanide-dependent enzyme XoxF (EC 1.1.2.10). The authors found that xoxF-linked methanol oxidation signals recur across wetland environments, suggesting this pathway is more widespread in wetlands than previously appreciated. The work highlights a relatively understudied aspect of wetland carbon cycling compared to methane oxidation.

papers.title: Rumen DNA virome plasticity and viral metabolic potential are associated with seasonal adaptation in grazing yak and cattle on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau.
papers.abstract: As a diverse and abundant component of the rumen ecosystem, viruses interact with other microorganisms and are thought to influence microbial metabolism and host productivity. However, how the rumen virome responds to seasonal fluctuations in extreme environments remains poorly understood. Here, metagenomic analyses were used to investigate temporal dynamics of viral diversity, functional potential, and virus-host associations in the rumen virome of yak and cattle on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau across warm and cold seasons.
papers.journal: Journal of animal science and biotechnology
papers.summary: This study used metagenomics to track how the rumen DNA virome of grazing yak and cattle on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau changes between warm and cold seasons. It found that viral diversity, functional potential, and virus-host interactions shift seasonally, with viruses carrying metabolic genes that may help the host microbiome adapt to extreme environmental fluctuations. The work links rumen virome plasticity to seasonal adaptation in these high-altitude ruminants.

papers.title: Decadal Resampling Reveals Widespread Increases in Soil Microbial Diversity Associated With Nitrogen Deposition.
papers.abstract: Simulated manipulation experiments, such as nitrogen addition to mimic atmospheric nitrogen deposition, are widely used in global change research. However, experimental manipulations may differ from real-world environmental change in their intensity, duration, and co-occurrence, leaving long-term changes in soil microbial communities and soil health insufficiently understood. To address this gap, we resampled soils from 38 forest and grassland ecosystems across eastern China in 2009 and 2019 and assessed microbial taxonomic and functional diversity using shotgun metagenomics. Microbial diversi
papers.summary: By resampling soils from 38 forest and grassland sites across eastern China a decade apart, the authors found that soil microbial taxonomic and functional diversity increased over time, and these increases were linked to nitrogen deposition. This suggests real-world nitrogen deposition may boost soil microbial diversity, contrasting with some short-term nitrogen-addition experiments.

papers.title: Major Depressive Disorder Signatures: A Review of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Powered Insights Into Gut Dysbiosis.
papers.abstract: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is a highly common neuropsychiatric disorder globally. A variety of factors contribute to the neuropathology of MDD. Microbiome research in neuropsychiatric disorders such as MDD has recently attracted attention. Indeed, the gut-brain axis could influence the course of MDD through metabolites such as Gamma-Aminobutyric Acid (GABA), Quinolinate, and other factors. Such metabolites may modulate the balance of excitatory and inhibitory signals. Moreover, MDD features abundant hyperinflammatory bacteria, whereas anti-inflammatory butyrate-synthesizing genera are dec
papers.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence approaches are being applied to understand the link between gut microbiome dysbiosis and Major Depressive Disorder. It highlights how gut-brain axis metabolites such as GABA and quinolinate may influence excitatory/inhibitory signaling, and notes that MDD is associated with increased hyperinflammatory bacteria and reduced anti-inflammatory butyrate-producing genera.

papers.title: Urinary microbiome in renal transplant patients with BK polyomavirus reactivation.
papers.abstract: Introduction. BK polyomavirus (BKPyV) reactivation is a significant health risk among renal transplant recipients that can lead to nephropathy and allograft loss.Hypothesis/Gap statement. While the microbiota is increasingly recognized as an important determinant of viral infection and pathogenesis, as well as itself undergoing compositional changes in response to infection, the urinary microbiome has yet to be investigated in the context of BK polyomavirus reactivation.Aim. This study aimed to investigate associations between the urinary microbiome and BKPyV-DNAemia in renal transplant patien
papers.summary: This study investigated the urinary microbiome in kidney transplant recipients to see whether its composition is associated with BK polyomavirus reactivation, a major cause of graft loss. The authors compared the urinary microbial communities of patients with and without BKPyV-DNAemia, identifying compositional differences linked to viral reactivation. The findings suggest the urinary microbiome may serve as a marker or contributing factor in BKPyV pathogenesis.

papers.title: Do individual or societal consequences matter more? Reducing antibiotic expectations for uncomplicated urinary tract infections in females.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is an urgent public health threat. Antibiotic prescriptions in primary care, such as for uncomplicated urinary tract infections (UTIs) in females, contribute substantially to antibiotic overuse. We examined whether consequence-based risk communication emphasizing either individual (gut microbiome disruption) or societal (AMR) consequences can reduce expectations to receive antibiotics and improve decision-related outcomes.
papers.summary: This study tests whether risk messages about antibiotic resistance work better when they emphasize personal consequences (like gut microbiome disruption) or societal consequences (like antimicrobial resistance). The goal is to reduce patient expectations for antibiotics in uncomplicated urinary tract infections, a common source of antibiotic overuse in primary care.

papers.title: A Narrative Review of Airway and Gut Microbiota in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: Clinical Associations, Methodological Heterogeneity, and Translational Priorities.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a heterogeneous disorder in which exacerbation susceptibility, persistent inflammation, disease progression, and treatment response are not fully explained by spirometry. Culture-independent studies have associated airway and gut microbial features with clinically relevant COPD phenotypes, but findings are highly sensitive to sampling site, low biomass, contamination control, sequencing depth and platform, bioinformatic workflow, microbial-load quantification, medication exposure, disease state, and host or environmental confounding. Methodologic
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence linking airway and gut microbiota to clinically relevant COPD phenotypes such as exacerbation susceptibility and inflammation, while emphasizing that findings are highly sensitive to methodological factors like sampling site, low biomass, contamination, sequencing platform, and medication exposure. It highlights the need for standardized methods and translational priorities to move microbiome research toward clinical utility in COPD.

papers.title: Modulatory Effect of the Alfalfa Polysaccharide Fraction II on Cyclophosphamide-Induced Immunosuppression in Mice.
papers.abstract: This study investigated the protective effects of alfalfa polysaccharide fraction II (APS-II) on immunosuppression induced by cyclophosphamide (CTX) in mice. APS-II was extracted using ultrasound-assisted enzymatic extraction method and purified by DEAE-52 cellulose chromatography. Its structural characteristics, including molecular weight (Mw), monosaccharide composition, and thermal stability, were analyzed. A CTX-induced immunosuppressed mouse model was established to evaluate the effects of APS-II on immune organ indices, serum cytokines, antioxidant indicators in liver and spleen tissues,
papers.summary: This study extracted and characterized a polysaccharide fraction (APS-II) from alfalfa and tested its protective effects in mice with cyclophosphamide-induced immunosuppression. APS-II improved immune organ indices, serum cytokines, and antioxidant markers in liver and spleen tissues, suggesting it may help counteract chemotherapy-related immune suppression.

papers.title: A Step-by-Step Guide to Successful Multiparametric Microbiota Flow Cytometry.
papers.abstract: The role of the human microbiota in host health is an important area of research. Conventional characterization of the complex microbial communities colonizing the human body is primarily performed using culture-based or high-throughput sequencing approaches, which have improved general understanding yet lack cellular features relevant for interaction and function at the single-cell level. Flow cytometry is an established tool for single-cell analysis, and recent improvements, such as increased resolution of small cells and particles, offer possibilities for characterizing complex microbial co
papers.summary: This protocol paper provides a detailed, step-by-step guide for performing multiparametric flow cytometry on complex microbial communities, addressing recent improvements in resolving small cells and particles. It aims to enable single-cell characterization of microbiota, complementing culture-based and sequencing methods by capturing cellular features relevant to host-microbe interactions.

papers.title: Soil microbial effects on tree seedling performance during forest secondary succession.
papers.abstract: Soil microbiota influence seedling survival and abundance in mature forests. However, their role in tree species turnover during secondary forest succession remains unclear, especially in species-rich tropical forests. We conducted a shade house experiment to assess variation in the direction and strength of net soil microbial effects on seedling emergence, biomass growth, and mortality of seven tree species. We tested for effects of soil successional stage (0, 15, 25, and 115 years of forest recovery), tree species' association with successional stages (home stages where species peak in abund
papers.summary: This study used a shade house experiment to test how soil microbiota from forests at different stages of secondary succession (0, 15, 25, and 115 years of recovery) affect seedling emergence, growth, and mortality of seven tropical tree species. The researchers examined whether microbial effects vary with soil successional stage and whether tree species perform better in soils from the successional stage where they are most abundant. The findings help clarify the role of soil microbes in driving tree species turnover during tropical forest recovery.

papers.title: Evaluation of a Lactobacillus biopreservative on milk cake quality: Effects on physicochemical, microbiological, and flavor properties.
papers.abstract: This study investigated the effectiveness of preservation films derived from two Lactobacillus biopreservatives in maintaining the freshness of milk cake. The biopreservatives, fermented whey and its cell-free supernatant (CFS), were produced synergistically by high-exopolysaccharide (EPS)-producing Limosilactobacillus fermentum A51 and high-phenyllactic acid (PLA)-producing Lactobacillus plantarum L3. Both biopreservatives, rich in EPS (412.91-429.33 mg/L) and PLA (69.24-70.55 mg/L), showed strong antioxidant and antibacterial activity. EPS formed a stable protective film on milk cake surface
papers.summary: This study developed biopreservative films from fermented whey and cell-free supernatant produced by two Lactobacillus strains (one high in exopolysaccharides, one high in phenyllactic acid) and tested them on milk cake. The films showed strong antioxidant and antibacterial activity and helped maintain the freshness of the milk cake. The work demonstrates a potential natural alternative to synthetic preservatives for dairy products.

papers.title: The Calcidiscus leptoporus genome reveals vitamin-mediated holobiont interactions.
papers.abstract: Coccolithophores are major marine phytoplankton that contribute to ocean carbon cycling through both organic carbon fixation and calcium carbonate biomineralization, yet the functional basis of their interactions with phycosphere bacteria remains poorly resolved. Here, we present the nuclear genome of the haploid phase of the coccolithophore Calcidiscus leptoporus, a coccolithophore that calcifies in both life-cycle stages. We combined host genome analysis, genome-resolved characterization of associated bacteria, and a four-month vitamin-manipulation experiment to test how B-vitamin biosynthet
papers.summary: Researchers sequenced the nuclear genome of the haploid phase of the coccolithophore Calcidiscus leptoporus, a marine phytoplankton important for ocean carbon cycling. By combining host genome analysis with genome-resolved characterization of associated bacteria and a four-month vitamin-manipulation experiment, they show that B-vitamin biosynthesis underpins interactions between the host and its phycosphere microbiome. The work reveals vitamin-mediated holobiont interactions in a globally significant calcifying phytoplankton lineage.

papers.title: Immune regulatory networks and gut microbiota-associated targets in endometriosis: an integrative multi-omics and network analysis.
papers.abstract: Endometriosis is an estrogen-dependent disorder characterized by chronic inflammation, immune dysregulation, and altered hormone metabolism. Although gut microbiota-derived metabolites have been implicated in shaping immune microenvironments and lesion development, the underlying regulatory mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we integrated multi-omics, protein-protein interaction (PPI), SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and single-cell transcriptomics to identify core targets and delineate their interactions with microbiota-derived metabolites, followed by molecular simulation
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics, protein-protein interaction networks, SHAP-based machine learning, and single-cell transcriptomics to identify core immune-regulatory targets in endometriosis and link them to gut microbiota-derived metabolites. The authors use molecular simulation to characterize these interactions, proposing candidate mechanisms connecting the microbiome to endometriosis-associated immune dysregulation.

papers.title: Metagenome-scale modeling to assess microbiome metabolic complementarity for precision microbiota transplantation therapies.
papers.abstract: Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) holds therapeutic promise beyond recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection, but clinical outcomes remain unpredictable and donor-selection strategies remain limited, in part because the role of donor‒recipient metabolic interactions in shaping the post-FMT community remains poorly understood. Here, we leverage metagenome-scale metabolic modeling to quantify metabolic niche complementarity between donor and recipient microbiomes and predict post-FMT community composition. Using MICOM-derived metabolic models, we show that donor genomes whose metabolic f
papers.summary: This study uses metagenome-scale metabolic modeling (MICOM) to quantify metabolic niche complementarity between donor and recipient microbiomes, aiming to predict post-FMT community composition and improve donor selection. The authors show that donor genomes whose metabolic capabilities complement the recipient's existing community may better engraft, offering a framework for precision microbiota transplantation.

papers.title: Towards optimizing the host response to biotics: a report of an International Scientific Association for Probiotics and Prebiotics working group.
papers.abstract: This report summarizes the deliberations of a working group convened by the International Scientific Association for Probiotics and Prebiotics (ISAPP) at their 2025 annual meeting to identify the key targets that mediate the host response to biotics. Probiotics, prebiotics, synbiotics, and postbiotics have been explored in numerous contexts, but results of clinical trials are mixed. In most studies performed to date, a therapeutic product and its dose and administration strategy were selected based on factors other than rigorous mechanistic evidence. Given recent advances in our understanding
papers.summary: This report summarizes an ISAPP working group's deliberations on identifying the key host targets that mediate responses to probiotics, prebiotics, synbiotics, and postbiotics. The authors argue that mixed clinical trial results stem from product and dosing choices made without rigorous mechanistic evidence, and they propose prioritizing mechanistic understanding to optimize future biotic interventions.

papers.title: Determinants of enteric hyperoxaluria in the SAMP1/YitFc mouse model of spontaneous ileitis.
papers.abstract: Enteric hyperoxaluria (EH) results from increased oxalate bioavailability in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract, often affecting patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). We investigated the pathophysiology of EH in an ileitis mouse model, hypothesizing that fat malabsorption, increased gut permeability, and microbial shifts collectively contribute to the hyperoxaluric phenotype in the setting of GI tract inflammation. SAMP1/YitFc (SAMP1) mice and their parental AKR controls were fed one of three diets varying in fat content (10%, 45%, or 60% kcal), each supplemented with 1% oxalate, for 6
papers.summary: This study investigates the causes of enteric hyperoxaluria (excess oxalate absorption leading to kidney stone risk) in SAMP1/YitFc mice, a model of spontaneous ileitis resembling Crohn's disease. The authors test whether fat malabsorption, increased gut permeability, and microbial changes together drive the hyperoxaluric phenotype across diets with varying fat content. The work links intestinal inflammation and diet composition to oxalate handling in the gut.

papers.title: Longitudinal development of infant oral ecosystem: salivary metabolomic, bacteriome, and virome dynamics in early infancy.
papers.abstract: This prospective cohort study investigated the longitudinal development of the salivary bacteriome, virome, and metabolome during early infancy. We assessed the associations between oral bacteria, viruses, and metabolites from 10 mother-infant dyads, with oral samples collected at 1 and 2 years of age. Forty saliva and plaque samples underwent untargeted metabolomic analysis, and infant saliva samples underwent metagenomic sequencing. Maternal salivary and plaque metabolomic profiles remained largely stable, whereas infant profiles were clearly separated from maternal profiles and changed with
papers.summary: This prospective cohort study tracked the salivary bacteriome, virome, and metabolome in 10 mother-infant pairs at 1 and 2 years of age, finding that infant oral profiles were distinct from maternal profiles and shifted over time, while maternal profiles remained stable. The work links bacterial, viral, and metabolic dynamics in the developing infant oral ecosystem.

papers.title: Development and Validation of Mock Communities as Quality Control Materials for Clinical Metagenomic Next-Generation Sequencing.
papers.abstract: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (NGS) enables comprehensive detection of a broad spectrum of microorganisms. However, its clinical application faces two major challenges: the development of appropriate microbiome-based biomarkers and the need to ensure the reproducibility and quality of the microbiome analytical workflow. Therefore, we developed four types of bead-based mock communities as standard materials for microbiome analysis and evaluated potential experimental biases arising from nucleic acid extraction and sequence analysis.
papers.summary: This study developed four bead-based mock communities to serve as quality control materials for clinical metagenomic next-generation sequencing, addressing the need for reproducible microbiome workflows. The authors evaluated biases introduced during nucleic acid extraction and sequence analysis, providing a standardized reference for validating microbiome analytical pipelines.

papers.title: Metagenomic insights into mechanisms of coral larval settlement induction and inhibition by marine biofilms.
papers.abstract: Biofilms are essential to larval settlement in many marine invertebrates, yet the mechanisms driving settlement induction or inhibition in corals remain poorly resolved. This challenge lies in the vast taxonomic and functional diversity of marine biofilms, making it difficult to identify cues associated with settlement. To address this, we analysed the metagenomes of biofilms used to induce settlement (attachment and metamorphosis) of four broadcast-spawning non-acroporid coral species: Dipsastrea favus, Platygyra sinensis, Echinophyllia aspera and Porites lobata. Biofilms were developed for o
papers.summary: This study used metagenomic sequencing of marine biofilms to identify the microbial taxa and functional genes associated with inducing or inhibiting larval settlement in four non-acroporid coral species. By comparing biofilms that promote attachment and metamorphosis versus those that do not, the authors link specific microbial community features and metabolic pathways to settlement cues. The work advances understanding of coral recruitment mechanisms, which is relevant for reef restoration and conservation.

papers.title: ESM2-Guided Context-Aware Annotation Completion Supplements Carbohydrate Metabolism Coverage in Silage Microbial Metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Functional annotation gaps limit the interpretation of carbohydrate metabolism in silage microbiomes. We developed Context-Aware Annotation Completion (CAAC), a framework integrating ESM2 embeddings, genomic-neighborhood features, three-class classification, confidence-tiered neighbor voting, and Enzyme Commission (EC)-to-KEGG Orthology (KO) mapping. CAAC was applied to 21 metagenomes from uninoculated and Lacticaseibacillus paracasei-inoculated silages sampled before ensiling and at 7 and 90 days. Five-fold cross-validation yielded an F1-macro of 84.64% for negative, positive, and hard-sequen
papers.summary: The authors developed CAAC, a framework that uses ESM2 protein language model embeddings combined with genomic-neighborhood features to fill in missing functional annotations in silage microbial metagenomes. Applied to 21 metagenomes from silage fermentation experiments, it improved coverage of carbohydrate metabolism genes, achieving an F1-macro of 84.64% in cross-validation. This addresses a common problem where many metagenomic genes lack functional labels, limiting metabolic interpretation.

papers.title: Precision Nutrigenomics in Cultured Finfish: Dietary Regulation of Gene Expression, Microbial Ecology, Metabolism, and Immunity.
papers.abstract: Precision nutrigenomics requires a diet-microbiome-host perspective because microorganisms can transform feed substrates, generate bioactive metabolites, compete with pathogens, and modify intestinal and systemic gene regulation. This structured narrative review synthesizes representative controlled feeding trials, transcriptomic and targeted gene-expression studies, microbiome analyses, and complementary multi-omic evidence concerning dietary regulations in cultured finfish. The available evidence is concentrated particularly on soybean-derived proteins, lipid-source replacements, selected am
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on how diet shapes gene expression, gut microbial ecology, metabolism, and immunity in cultured finfish, emphasizing a diet-microbiome-host framework. It focuses on common feed substitutions such as soybean-derived proteins and alternative lipid sources, highlighting transcriptomic and microbiome data from controlled feeding trials. The authors argue that precision nutrigenomics in aquaculture requires integrating multi-omic layers to optimize fish health and production.

papers.title: A Pan-European Whole-Microbiome Study of Wastewater Influent: Prokaryotes, Protists, Fungi, and Metazoa.
papers.abstract: Microbial communities entering wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) through untreated sewage represent an important interface between human, environmental, and treatment-associated microbiomes, yet our understanding of their biogeography remains poorly resolved, particularly for microbial eukaryotes. Using shotgun metagenomic time-series data from influent samples of seven WWTPs across a European latitudinal gradient, we analyzed the taxonomic composition and dynamics of bacteria, protists, fungi, and microscopic metazoa. Influent community composition varied with geographic location and season
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic time-series data from seven wastewater treatment plants across a European latitudinal gradient to characterize the full microbiome of untreated sewage influent, including bacteria, protists, fungi, and microscopic metazoa. The authors found that influent community composition varied with both geographic location and season, providing a broader view of wastewater microbial biogeography beyond bacteria alone.

papers.title: Lesion-specific oral microbiome signatures and predicted carcinogenic pathways in oral squamous cell carcinoma: a paired-site study in Pakistan.
papers.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma accounts for over 90% of oral neoplasms. Despite therapeutic advances, the lack of reliable, non-invasive biomarkers and delayed diagnosis continues to impede effective clinical management. By combining paired lesion and non-lesion sampling with predictive metagenomics analysis, our study addresses this gap and advances the current understanding of microbiome‒tumor interactions.
papers.summary: This study compared the oral microbiome at tumor sites versus matched non-lesion sites in patients with oral squamous cell carcinoma in Pakistan, identifying lesion-specific bacterial signatures. Using predictive metagenomic analysis, the authors also inferred microbial pathways that may contribute to carcinogenesis, suggesting the oral microbiome could serve as a non-invasive biomarker source.

papers.title: Ecological assembly of mucosal and fecal microbiomes in ulcerative colitis across genes, functions, and species.
papers.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is associated with gut microbial dysbiosis, yet the ecological processes underlying community assembly remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study investigates the ecological processes that shape gut microbial communities in ulcerative colitis by comparing mucosal and fecal microbiomes across taxonomic, functional, and strain-level (species) resolution. It aims to clarify how dysbiosis arises through community assembly mechanisms rather than just describing taxonomic shifts. The work provides a framework for understanding microbiome ecology in IBD.

papers.title: Multi-layer gut microbiome variation in type 2 diabetes despite preserved higher-order community structure.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) has been consistently associated with alterations in the gut microbiome, although disease, treatment, diet, and other host factors may contribute to the observed patterns. How these associations are organized across different biological levels of the microbial ecosystem remains incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study examines how the gut microbiome differs in type 2 diabetes across multiple biological levels, from individual taxa to overall community organization. Despite finding layer-specific microbial variation associated with T2D, the higher-order community structure appears largely preserved, suggesting that disease-related shifts occur within a stable ecological framework. The work highlights the importance of multi-level analyses when interpreting microbiome-disease associations.

papers.title: Using nanopore metagenomics to characterize pathogens in febrile patients from a highland of Western Kenya.
papers.abstract: Febrile illness remains a leading cause of morbidity in sub-Saharan Africa despite substantial reductions in malaria transmission. As malaria positive cases decrease, an increasing number of patients with febrile illnesses test negative for Plasmodium infection, leaving their causes unresolved. As a result of the diagnostic gap, patients receive presumptive antimalarial treatment, unnecessary antibiotics and experience delayed therapy.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study applies nanopore metagenomic sequencing to identify pathogens in febrile patients from a highland region of Western Kenya, where declining malaria cases leave many fevers without a diagnosed cause. The approach aims to close this diagnostic gap by detecting diverse pathogens directly from patient samples, potentially reducing unnecessary antimalarial and antibiotic treatment.

papers.title: Agentic AI for trustworthy synthetic microbial genomics: a perspective on generation, validation, and governance.
papers.abstract: Synthetic microbial genomic data are becoming increasingly important for benchmarking microbial genome analysis pipelines, simulating rare taxa, evaluating metagenomic workflows, and supporting reproducible computational biology. Recent genomic foundation models demonstrate that biological sequences can be modelled at unprecedented scale, with emerging capacity for genome-level interpretation, generation, and design. However, the scientific value of synthetic microbial genomic data depends not only on whether sequences can be generated, but whether they are biologically plausible, computationa
papers.summary: This perspective article discusses how agentic AI systems could be used to generate synthetic microbial genomic data that is biologically plausible and computationally useful for benchmarking and simulation. It emphasizes that generation alone is insufficient, and proposes frameworks for validation and governance to ensure trustworthiness. The paper is a conceptual roadmap rather than a primary research study.

papers.title: Beyond antibiotics: artificial intelligence-enabled anti-infective ecosystems for next-generation precision therapeutics against antimicrobial resistance.
papers.abstract: The rapid global expansion of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) threatens to undermine decades of progress in infectious disease management and highlights the limitations of conventional antibiotic-centered therapeutic strategies. Although emerging technologies-including antimicrobial peptides, bacteriophage therapy, CRISPR-based antimicrobials, microbiome therapeutics, anti-virulence approaches, nanotechnology-enabled drug delivery, and artificial intelligence (AI)-have individually demonstrated considerable promise, they are predominantly being developed as independent interventions rather than
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This review argues that antimicrobial resistance cannot be solved by conventional antibiotics alone and proposes integrating diverse emerging technologies—antimicrobial peptides, phage therapy, CRISPR antimicrobials, microbiome therapeutics, anti-virulence strategies, nanotech delivery, and AI—into a unified 'anti-infective ecosystem.' The key contribution is a conceptual framework for AI-enabled precision therapeutics that combines these approaches rather than developing them in isolation.

papers.title: Integrative artificial intelligence and multi-omics modeling approach for characterizing microbial dynamics and health impacts in space microgravity and radiation conditions.
papers.abstract: Characterizing microbial dynamics and their potential health impacts under space microgravity and radiation conditions remains a major challenge in space biology. The complexity of microbial adaptation, host associated microbiome variation, and heterogeneous multi omics responses requires computational methods that can jointly model temporal dynamics, biological interactions, and predictive uncertainty.
papers.summary: This paper proposes an integrative AI and multi-omics modeling framework to characterize how microbial communities adapt and affect health under space microgravity and radiation conditions. It aims to jointly model temporal dynamics, biological interactions, and predictive uncertainty, addressing a key challenge in space biology.

papers.title: Effects of electroacupuncture on neurological outcomes and brain-gut axis-associated changes in experimental ischemic stroke models: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Ischemic stroke is a leading cause of death and disability worldwide and is frequently accompanied by brain-gut axis disturbances, including intestinal barrier dysfunction, gut microbiota dysbiosis, and immune-inflammatory imbalance. Although electroacupuncture (EA) has demonstrated neuroprotective effects in experimental stroke, its effects on brain-gut axis-related outcomes have not been systematically evaluated.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates whether electroacupuncture improves neurological outcomes and brain-gut axis-related measures (intestinal barrier function, gut microbiota, and immune-inflammatory balance) in experimental ischemic stroke models. It synthesizes preclinical evidence to assess the consistency and magnitude of these effects across studies.

papers.title: Microbial enzyme-responsive inulin nanoparticles for colon-targeted oral delivery of 5-ASA toward improved therapy of inflammatory bowel disease.
papers.abstract: Colon-targeted delivery of 5-aminosalicylic acid (5-ASA) offers an effective strategy for treating inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) while minimizing systemic side effects. However, conventional oral 5-ASA formulations suffer from premature drug release and poor colon specificity. To overcome these limitations, we developed a biodegradable, prebiotic, and immunomodulatory inulin nanoparticle (INP) platform enabling microbial enzyme-responsive and site-specific release of 5-ASA in the colon.
papers.summary: This paper describes an inulin nanoparticle platform that carries the IBD drug 5-ASA and releases it specifically in the colon in response to microbial enzymes. The prebiotic and immunomodulatory nature of inulin may also provide additional therapeutic benefits beyond drug delivery. This approach aims to improve IBD treatment while reducing systemic side effects from premature drug release.

papers.title: Effect of quorum quenching enzyme YtnP on immune response and intestinal microbiota in Aeromonas hydrophila-infected grass carp (Ctenopharyngodon idella).
papers.abstract: Aeromonas hydrophila induces tissue swelling, necrosis, ulcers, and hemorrhagic septicemia in grass carp, causing significant economic losses. Quorum sensing, a communication mechanism among microorganisms, plays a key role in microbial ecological competition and dynamic equilibrium. Quorum quenching has emerged as a hot spot in anti-bacterial infection research. In this study, grass carp (n = 75 per group) were intraperitoneally injected with A. hydrophila and the quorum quenching enzyme YtnP. The expression levels of immune-related genes were assessed by qPCR. The intestinal microbiota was s
papers.summary: This study investigated whether the quorum quenching enzyme YtnP can protect grass carp from Aeromonas hydrophila infection by modulating immune gene expression and gut microbiota. The authors injected fish with the pathogen and enzyme, then measured immune-related gene expression via qPCR and characterized intestinal microbial communities. The findings suggest that YtnP influences both the host immune response and microbiome composition during infection.

papers.title: Integrating Plant Physiology and Microbiome Engineering for Climate-Resilient Crops: Bridging Knowledge Gaps in Multi-Stress Tolerance.
papers.abstract: Climate change is intensifying the frequency and co-occurrence of abiotic and biotic stresses, posing significant challenges to global crop productivity and stability. Conventional approaches based on single-stress responses are increasingly insufficient for addressing complex field environments where plants experience multiple simultaneous stresses. This review synthesizes current knowledge on plant physiological responses, microbiome interactions, and emerging technological interventions to develop an integrative framework for climate-resilient agriculture. It highlights how stress perceptio
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on how plants physiologically respond to co-occurring abiotic and biotic stresses and how the plant microbiome can be engineered to improve tolerance. It proposes an integrative framework combining plant physiology and microbiome engineering to develop climate-resilient crops, highlighting gaps in understanding multi-stress tolerance.

papers.title: Exposure-aware multi-omics and artificial intelligence for biomarker discovery and precision prevention in diffuse glioma.
papers.abstract: Diffuse gliomas are now diagnosed and studied through integrated molecular classification, radiomics, single-cell biology, spatial profiling, proteogenomics, metabolomics, and artificial intelligence. Yet many precision-medicine models still begin at diagnosis and emphasize tumor-intrinsic molecular features, leaving environmental, occupational, lifestyle, microbiome, metabolic, immune, and treatment-related exposures at the margins. This review develops an exposome-informed view of diffuse glioma biomarker discovery. Biomarker discovery is separated from clinical prevention: current evidence
papers.summary: This review argues that diffuse glioma research and precision medicine have focused too narrowly on tumor-intrinsic molecular features at diagnosis, overlooking environmental, occupational, lifestyle, microbiome, metabolic, immune, and treatment-related exposures. It proposes an exposome-informed framework that integrates multi-omics, radiomics, single-cell and spatial profiling, and AI to discover biomarkers for earlier precision prevention rather than only post-diagnosis treatment.

papers.title: Decoding the functional diversity of plant growth-promoting bacterial communities in the soils of Western Ghats, Tamil Nadu, India.
papers.abstract: Western ghats in India, one of the world's biodiversity hot spots is the reservoirs of microbial resources having agricultural and industrial significance. However, the diversity of plant growth-promoting microbial communities associated with the plants and soil in the Western Ghats is untapped vault. The current emphasis on natural farming is more depending on the indigenous microbial communities and their metabolic functions towards sustainable one -health. With this background, the present study examines the bacterial diversity of soils from the Western Ghats of Nilgiris, Coimbatore and Din
papers.summary: This study surveys bacterial communities in soils from the Western Ghats biodiversity hotspot in Tamil Nadu, India, focusing on plant growth-promoting bacteria with potential agricultural value. It characterizes the functional diversity of these indigenous microbial communities, which remain largely unexplored despite growing interest in natural farming and sustainable agriculture.

papers.title: Gut microbiota-derived metabolites target C5AR1/KDM2A/HCAR3 axis in inflammatory bowel disease: a multi-machine learning algorithms and molecular docking study.
papers.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic recurrent disorder. Gut microbiota-derived metabolites regulate intestinal homeostasis, but their molecular mechanisms in IBD remain unclear. Current studies lack systematic "microbiota-metabolite-target" network mining with multi-method validation. This study integrates network pharmacology, three machine learning algorithms, and molecular docking to construct this regulatory network in IBD.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study integrates network pharmacology, three machine learning algorithms, and molecular docking to construct a 'microbiota-metabolite-target' regulatory network in inflammatory bowel disease, identifying a C5AR1/KDM2A/HCAR3 axis as a potential key pathway. The work suggests that gut microbiota-derived metabolites may influence IBD pathogenesis through these targets, providing candidate mechanisms for further experimental validation.

papers.title: Gut microbiota profiles and potential biomarkers in pre-pubertal females with ADHD.
papers.abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a highly prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder with significant sex differences in diagnostic rates; males being diagnosed more frequently than females. Gut microbiota alterations may contribute to ADHD via the microbiota-gut-brain axis. However, previous microbiota studies have predominantly used male or mixed-gender samples, neglecting females with distinct clinical and hormonal profiles. The pre-pubertal period is critical for both neurodevelopment and microbiota maturation. This study investigates gut microbiota characteristics in pre-pube
papers.summary: This study characterizes gut microbiota profiles in pre-pubertal females with ADHD, a group largely overlooked in prior microbiome research that focused on males or mixed-gender samples. The authors identify potential microbial biomarkers associated with ADHD in this specific population, highlighting the importance of sex- and developmental-stage-specific analyses in microbiota-gut-brain axis research.

papers.title: Fighting the invader: strategies against intracellular bacteria.
papers.abstract: Intracellular pathogenic bacteria are often-overlooked agent of chronic, recurrent and difficult-to-treat infections in a context of escalating antimicrobial resistance. By hiding within professional and non-professional phagocytes, adopting dormant or slow-replicative states and rewiring host pathways, these pathogens successfully evade both immune clearance and conventional antibiotic therapy, thus contributing to treatment failure and, potentially, carcinogenesis. Here we synthesise how obligate and facultative intracellular bacteria invade and persist within host cells, and interpret these
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how obligate and facultative intracellular bacteria invade host cells, persist in dormant or slow-replicating states, and evade both immune clearance and conventional antibiotics. It highlights these pathogens as underappreciated causes of chronic, recurrent, hard-to-treat infections amid rising antimicrobial resistance, and discusses strategies to counter them.

papers.title: Hormone priming and metabolic engineering of phytohormone crosstalk in rice under combined biotic and abiotic stresses: a multi-omics perspective for climate-resilient crop development.
papers.abstract: Rice (Oryza sativa L.) is the caloric backbone for more than half of humanity, yet it remains one of the most vulnerable crops to the simultaneous biotic and abiotic stresses exacerbated by climate change. Phytohormone priming and the complex crosstalk networks governed by transcription factor hubs like WRKY, MYB, and NAC serve as the central adaptive mechanism for stress resilience. This review synthesizes how multi-omics integration, including spatial and single-cell transcriptomics, is resolving the molecular architecture of hormonal priming and epigenetic stress memory. We critically evalu
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how phytohormone priming and crosstalk networks governed by WRKY, MYB, and NAC transcription factors mediate rice resilience to combined biotic and abiotic stresses. It highlights how multi-omics integration, including spatial and single-cell transcriptomics, is uncovering the molecular architecture of hormonal priming and epigenetic stress memory to guide climate-resilient crop development.

papers.title: Lactobacillus acidophilus CICC 22162 alleviates sleep deprivation-induced cognitive impairment by remodeling gut microbiota and enhancing S-adenosylmethionine-mediated neuroimmune regulation.
papers.abstract: Sleep deprivation (SD) impairs cognitive function and induces hippocampal injury, yet the gut-derived mechanisms underlying these deficits remain incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study shows that supplementing with Lactobacillus acidophilus CICC 22162 in sleep-deprived animals reduces cognitive impairment and hippocampal injury. The protective effect appears to work by reshaping the gut microbiome and boosting S-adenosylmethionine-mediated neuroimmune regulation.
